project.domain: clinical context, interoperability and bounded clinical agents

thesis: An AI agent is a separately identified delegated principal; patient, encounter, tool, data, egress and clinical authority remain outside the model.

evidence.claim: Agent operations are evaluated against an explicit delegated authority envelope.
Agents are never clinicians or systems of record and cannot grant themselves authority.
Delegations bind exact patient, encounter, tools, operations, data categories and ceilings.
Delegated tool and operation boundaries are regression tested.
Organisation and patient context isolation are explicit production requirements.
Patient/task-scoped gateway behavior is tested in the synthetic runtime.
Consequential clinical operations require explicit human confirmation; write-back remains separately gated.
Human authority remains final and clinical production write-back is blocked.
CareOS preserves source identity, provenance, time, lifecycle and freshness.
Source-linked agent results remain inside patient/task boundaries.
PHI egress, credentials, arbitrary URLs, broad patient search and unrestricted MCP access are denied by policy.
Hijacking and protected-data access attempts are adversarially tested.
Delegations include hard limits for tool calls, records, pages, runtime and sub-agent depth.
Expired, excessive and out-of-envelope behavior is tested.
Audit requirements distinguish human delegator, agent version, patient/task scope, tools, authorization decisions and outcomes.
The containment suite produces inspectable attack/result evidence when generated in CI or locally.
Models, MCP servers, plugins and connectors are treated as non-implicitly-trusted supply-chain components.
Malicious tool/content behavior is included in agent security tests.
Six synthetic compromised-worker attack cases test deterministic containment.
The red-team containment suite is regression tested.
A machine-readable containment report can be generated from the same suite.
Security-relevant audit, rate, blast-radius and kill-switch requirements are specified.
Identifiable production use remains blocked; real production security telemetry is not claimed.

adversarial.taxonomy: CareOS clinical-agent containment suite aligned to agent hijacking, exfiltration, excessive agency and tool misuse

residualRisks: All CareOS agent production gates A0-A9 remain NOT PASS for identifiable live clinical use.
The six-case suite uses a deterministic compromised synthetic worker, not a live frontier model.
Organisation/workload identity, signed delegation and deployment-specific PHI egress controls require real environment evidence.
Independent clinical safety, privacy and security review is required before identifiable production use.
The separate frozen clinical-truth holdout remains a blocker for production correctness and must not be confused with a security pass.
